compareCandidate.label: Table vs. bar chart
compareCandidate.description: A table lists numbers precisely, row by row; a bar chart shows the same numbers as heights you can compare at a glance.

plainLanguageExplanation: A table organizes data points into rows (going across) and columns (going down), with a header that names each column. A class table might have one column for names and one for scores — each row is one student. To read a value, trace down to the right row and across to the right column. Tables make data exact, sortable, and easy to compare, and their numbers often feed straight into charts and statistics.

whyItMatters: Tables are the standard way the world stores and shares data — from sports stats to nutrition labels to bank statements. Reading a table is a daily life skill.
tagline: Data in neat rows and columns
didYouKnow: Nutrition labels, bus timetables, and sports scoreboards are all tables — millions of people read tables every day without ever calling them 'data tables'.
compareReason: Students see charts and tables as interchangeable — comparing the exact numbers with the visual heights shows when each shines.
